1	# local-whisper — Agent Guidelines
2	
3	## Project overview
4	
5	local-whisper is a fully-local macOS dictation tool. Hold **fn + left Control** to record, release to transcribe and insert text at cursor. Powered by whisper.cpp (C/C++, no Python) and Hammerspoon.
6	
7	## Architecture
8	
9	```
10	Hammerspoon eventtap (trigger combo hold/release, matched on raw device flags)
11	  → lw-record (native AVAudioEngine capture, 1s WAV chunks)
12	  ↓  streaming pipeline: every 3s, dispatch any pause-bounded ≤55s segment already on disk
13	  → ffmpeg concat → whisper-cli (chosen model — or the remote API), several may run at once
14	  ↓  (key released) → only the tail segment is left to transcribe
15	  → Post-processing (filler removal, app-aware capitalize)
16	  → Action hooks (voice commands, note-taking, app launching)
17	  → Text insertion at cursor (paste or keystroke)
18	  → Overlay + menu bar updates
19	```
20	
21	Transcription **is** pipelined: segments are sent to whisper while the user is still
22	talking, so the wait after release does not scale with the recording length. Text is still
23	only inserted once every segment is back — there are no live partials on screen. Older docs
24	claiming "nothing is transcribed until the key is released" describe the gap between
25	`ac4c275` (which deleted the pipeline) and its restoration; see the streaming section below.
26	
27	Everything runs inside `~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` — no external bash scripts at runtime.
28	The one compiled helper is `lw-record`; init.lua builds it on load when it is missing or
29	older than its source, so there is still no install step.
30	
31	## Key paths
32	
33	- `~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` — main config (overlay, recording, insertion, hotkeys, menu bar)
34	- `~/.hammerspoon/local_whisper_actions.lua` — user voice commands (optional, auto-reloads)
35	- `tools/lw-record.swift` — native mic recorder source (the only thing that opens the mic)
36	- `~/.local-whisper/bin/lw-record` — the compiled recorder, built by init.lua on load
37	- `~/.local-whisper/` — all user settings (lang, model, output, prompt, recent dictations)
38	- `~/.local-whisper/prompt` — mixed-language style anchor; seeded with a default on first run
39	- `~/whisper.cpp/build/bin/whisper-cli` — transcription binary
40	- `~/whisper.cpp/models/` — whisper models (medium, large-v3-turbo, etc.)
41	- `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/` — all temp state (per-user private dir on macOS)
42	- `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/chunks/` — recording segments (ephemeral)
43	- `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log` — debug log
44	
45	## Audio capture: never go back to ffmpeg for the microphone
46	
47	ffmpeg's avfoundation **input device** hands over roughly 90% of what it captures. Measured
48	with a fixed output duration: a `-t 20` run took 21.11s of wall clock, ffmpeg reported a
49	20.00s timeline, and the file held **18.04s** of PCM. Every 1-second chunk it wrote came out
50	0.885–0.917s long, so the loss is spread evenly — about 100ms missing from every second.
51	That swallows short words whole and clips longer ones, and because whisper is generative it
52	papers over the gaps with fluent invented text. The transcript reads *better* than the truth
53	while missing words, which is exactly what makes it hard to notice.
54	
55	None of these changed it: `-thread_queue_size`, `-drop_late_frames false`,
56	`-use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1`, `-capture_raw_data true`, `-audio_device_index`, `:0` vs
57	`:default`, dropping the segment muxer, or dropping the resampler (native 48kHz loses the
58	same). It is inside the indev.
59	
60	`tools/lw-record.swift` taps AVAudioEngine's input node instead and loses nothing: chunks
61	come out at exactly `1.000000` s. ffmpeg is still correct — and still used — for segment
62	concat here and for all format conversion in `tools/transcribe.sh`. **Only the microphone
63	moved.** The `capture` checks in the test suite fail if `"avfoundation"` reappears as an
64	argument in init.lua.
65	
66	Verify capture health any time — the log line is written after every recording:
67	
68	```bash
69	TMPDIR_REAL=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)
70	grep "recording: captured" "${TMPDIR_REAL}whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log" | tail -3
71	# → recording: captured 19.54s of 20.11s wall (97%)
72	# Anything near 90% means capture regressed. The remainder is device-open latency.
73	```
74	
75	`lw-record` prints `READY` when its engine is actually running and `CAPTURED <secs>` on exit.
76	Both arrive on **stdout via the streaming callback** — `hs.task` routes stdout there whenever
77	a streaming callback is registered and leaves the termination callback's `out` empty, so
78	parsing `CAPTURED` at termination silently reads nil forever.
79	
80	## Conventions
81	
82	- Single-file architecture: all runtime logic in init.lua
83	- Hammerspoon API: `hs.canvas` for overlay, `hs.eventtap` for key detection and typing, `hs.pasteboard` for paste mode, `hs.task` for async processes, `hs.menubar` for status icon
84	- whisper.cpp binary is `whisper-cli`, NOT `main`
85	- No Python anywhere — this is a pure C/Lua stack
86	- Log to `$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log` for debugging
87	
88	## Development & Deployment
89	
90	### Deployment model (symlink — no copy needed)
91	
92	`~/.hammerspoon/init.lua` is a symlink pointing to `hammerspoon/init.lua` in this repo.
93	**Editing the repo file IS deployment.** There is no copy or install step.
94	
95	```bash
96	ls -la ~/.hammerspoon/init.lua
97	# → … -> /Users/vitaliy/Documents/GitHub/local-whisper/hammerspoon/init.lua
98	```
99	
100	### Syntax validation (before every reload)
101	
102	Use Hammerspoon's own Lua 5.4 compiler via the `hs` IPC bridge — no external tool needed:
103	
104	```bash
105	hs -c 'local f,e=loadfile(os.getenv("HOME").."/Documents/GitHub/local-whisper/hammerspoon/init.lua"); return f and "SYNTAX OK" or ("ERR: "..tostring(e))'
106	```
107	
108	`loadfile()` compiles without executing — it is safe to call on a live config.
109	Expected success output: `SYNTAX OK`
110	On error: `ERR: <file>:<line>: <message>`
111	
112	### Live reload
113	
114	```bash
115	hs -c "hs.reload()"
116	```
117	
118	Expected output includes `"Message port invalidated."` — this is **normal**; the Hammerspoon process restarts its IPC listener and the connection drops. Wait ~2s for reload to complete, then re-run the syntax check or test commands.
119	
120	### Lua 200-local-per-function hard ceiling
121	
122	Lua 5.4 (Hammerspoon's runtime) enforces a **hard limit of 200 locals per function**. The top-level chunk of `init.lua` counts as one function. This limit is a compiler error — exceeding it prevents the file from loading at all.
123	
124	**Current count: ~134/200** — comfortable headroom after meeting mode, LLM refine, silence auto-stop and preferred languages were removed. Only *top-level* locals count against the limit; locals inside a function body belong to that function's own budget, so match the start of the line exactly:
125	
126	```bash
127	grep -c '^local ' hammerspoon/init.lua
128	```
129	
130	**Rule**: Never add a new top-level `local` without first verifying the count stays ≤ 200. If the count climbs back toward the ceiling, group related state into a single table rather than adding bare locals — `finalizeTimers` (`{ timer, watchdog }`) and `TRIGGERS` (per-trigger `{ mask, label }`) are the existing examples of that pattern.
131	
132	### Declaration order matters as much as the count
133	
134	A `local` is only in scope for code that appears *after* its declaration. A function defined earlier in the file that references the name does **not** capture it — the reference silently compiles to a global lookup that reads `nil` at runtime, with no error at load time. This produced three separate live bugs in the overlay code (X button, unpin, pinning from the menu bar).
135	
136	`overlayPinned`, `isRecording`, and the `hideOverlay` forward declaration therefore sit **above** `createOverlay`, whose mouse callback closes over all three. When adding state that a callback touches, declare it above every function that references it.
